fields.meta_description: See four SEO automation examples an SEO team runs each week: ranking drops, broken links, content refreshes, and title checks. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build SEO Automation for Ranking Drops and Broken Links
fields.hero_description: Build SEO automation that flags ranking drops, lists broken links, and holds drafts until their titles fit.
fields.features_heading: Built on the Data Your SEO Team Trusts
fields.features_subheading: SEO automation is the process of using tools and software to perform repetitive, time-consuming SEO tasks on your own search data.
fields.feature_1:
Rules you write in plain English

You describe each check and who hears about it, such as "a drop of 5 places goes to the page owner." Emergent builds the app and its database, and you change a rule by prompting.
fields.feature_2:
Reads from the tools your rankings live in

The app connects to any tool with an API, such as Search Console or your CMS, and syncs data in and out. Each check runs on the same numbers your team already reports on.
fields.feature_3:
Each alert names the page and its owner

Alerts go out in Slack or by email, addressed to the person who owns the page. If nobody acts within the time you set, a reminder escalates to the SEO lead for that site.
fields.feature_4:
One record per URL, in a database you own

Every URL, its target query, its owner, and its last refresh date sit in a database you own. The dashboard updates live, and each open task sits beside the page it is about.
fields.feature_5:
No task cap on a site with 4,000 pages

Checking every page on a large site every day adds up to a lot of runs. Emergent sets no task cap on automation, and a daily check of 4,000 pages keeps running all month.
fields.feature_6:
Every rule, readable in your repository

On paid plans, Emergent exports the app's full code to your GitHub repository. A developer on your team can read exactly how a page gets flagged, assigned, or held back.

fields.usecase_heading: Four SEO Checks That Run on Their Own
fields.tab_content_1:
The guide lost 8 places, and its owner hears that day

The expense policy guide sat at average position 4 for its main query last week, and today it sits at 12. A drop of 8 places passes your 5-place limit. The daily check reads both positions through the Search Console API, opens task SEO-214, and sends the page owner, Ottilie Ekström, a direct message with both numbers.
fields.tab_content_2:
7 links to a deleted post, one fix list

Monday's site crawl turns up 7 internal links that point to /blog/2023-pricing, a post that now returns a 404. The app groups them by the article each one sits in and assigns the fix list to the web editor, Joaquim Carvalho. Links to live pages stay off the list.
fields.tab_content_3:
After 420 lost clicks, the checklist is due for a refresh

The remote onboarding checklist earned 1,200 clicks in the previous 90 days and 780 in the last 90 days. That is 420 lost clicks, past your limit of 300. The app adds the checklist to the refresh queue and assigns it to Bastien Leclercq, with both totals shown on the task.
fields.tab_content_4:
With a 71-character title, the draft stays unpublished

Funmi Adebayo's draft on onboarding small teams is ready to go, but its title tag runs 71 characters against your 60-character limit, and it has no meta description. The app keeps the draft out of the publish queue and sends Funmi a direct message listing both fixes.

fields.howto_description: Follow these seven steps to turn the checks your team runs by hand into SEO automation with real limits and named owners.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 List the checks your team repeats
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Write each limit as a number
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Name the source of each metric
fields.howto_step_1_des: Export a month of your team's SEO tasks and group them by kind, such as ranking reviews or link fixes. Mark the kinds that end the same way every time, and build those first.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Write the limit as a number the app can test: "5 places in a week", not "a big drop", and "60 characters", not "too long". A check with a number runs without anyone reading the report.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Note where each number comes from: average position and clicks from Search Console, titles from your CMS. Point the app at that source, never at a spreadsheet someone copied last month.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Put the checks, their limits, and who hears about each one into a single prompt. Emergent builds the app with its database and dashboard, and connects to each of your tools through its API.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Add an owner column to the page list before the first alert goes out. One named person per URL keeps a drop out of a shared inbox, and a second name covers vacations.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Run last quarter's positions and clicks through the app before it messages anyone. Compare its flags with what your team caught by hand, and adjust any limit that fires too often or too late.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Start with the checks that only flag and assign. Once the alerts have run for a month without a false one, let the app hold drafts out of the publish queue on its own.

faq_plan.a: It is the use of software to perform the repetitive, time-consuming tasks in SEO that someone would otherwise do by hand. Think of the checks your team runs every week: pages that slipped in rankings, internal links that broke, articles that lost clicks. Keep the work that needs judgment, such as choosing what to write next, with your team.

faq_plan.q: How do I set up SEO automation?
faq_plan.a: Start with one check your team already runs every week, such as a ranking review, and describe it in Emergent's AI automation builder: the data it reads, the limit that triggers it, and who hears about it. Emergent's free tier is enough to build and publish it. Add the next check to the same app with another prompt.

faq_plan.q: What are SEO automation tools used for?
faq_plan.a: They are used to take over the repeated SEO tasks that your team would otherwise do by hand. List your own repeated checks first, then compare each option against that list. With Emergent, the app you build reads rankings straight from the tool that holds them, through its API.

An SEO workflow is the order a page moves through, with one owner at each step: research, draft, edit, publish, and a review of how it ranks a month later. Write yours down before automating any of it. Keep SEO and marketing automation apart where the owners differ: when a page exists to bring in leads, the handoff to sales belongs in a sales automation.

faq_plan.q: Which checks should I automate first with SEO automation software?
faq_plan.a: Automate the checks your team repeats most that always end in the same action, such as a page that drops past a set number of places or a title over your length limit. Leave content decisions until later. For local SEO automation, use the same approach per location, with one page list and one owner for each.

faq_plan.q: What are the best SEO automation tools for an in-house team?
faq_plan.a: The best SEO automation tools for an in-house team read the data you already report on and reach each page's owner directly. Test each option on a month of your own positions and clicks, and count the alerts your team would have acted on. Drop any option whose alerts you would mostly ignore.

faq_plan.q: Do I need an SEO automation platform or are scripts enough?
faq_plan.a: Scripts are enough while only their author reads the output. Move to an SEO automation platform once more than one person acts on the checks. The rules and their owners then sit where everyone can see them. If the same team schedules posts, build that as its own social media automation with its own owners.

Here it means automating the checks around your articles, not the writing itself: one check on each draft before it publishes, and one on each published article's clicks afterward. A draft with a title over your limit waits, and an article that loses clicks goes back to a writer. The writing and the judgment about what to fix stay with people.

faq_plan.q: What is the best SEO automation software for a growing site?
faq_plan.a: The best SEO automation software for a growing site is one whose cost and limits still hold as your page count climbs. Check the price of each run, what the tool does when you reach its cap, and whether you can take the rules with you. Automation on Emergent has no task cap, and paid plans include a full code export to GitHub.

faq_plan.q: Can I build SEO automation with Python?
faq_plan.a: Yes. The Search Console API gives programmatic access to the most popular Search Console reports, and its query method exposes the Performance report's data, including clicks and average position. Google's Python quickstart needs Python 3 and a verified site. When drafts start to need an editor's sign-off, give that step its own content approval workflow.
